title: Lesson Six: Work to Learn - Don't Work for Money
coreMove: Choose work by learning yield as well as pay, so deep expertise gains the sales, money, systems, and people skills that make assets possible.

exampleSpecs.audience: creative professionals who rely on talent alone
exampleSpecs.stakes: become visible to buyers or keep treating selling as beneath the craft
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: a Singapore reporter resists a sales course while wanting bestselling results

exampleSpecs.stakes: train fear of rejection or stay protected from the skill that transfers
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the protagonist treats Xerox sales calls as four years of rejection training

exampleSpecs.stakes: make a pressure call or hide behind technical competence
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: military service teaches leadership under pressure with teams

exampleSpecs.audience: specialists with strong income but weak ownership skills
exampleSpecs.stakes: add money skills or keep needing an employer for every opportunity
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: specialization can create dependency when sales and financial skills are missing

exampleSpecs.audience: new managers who think management means giving orders
exampleSpecs.stakes: learn the whole system or mistake supervision for management
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: management includes cash flow, systems, and people

exampleSpecs.audience: workers comparing salary against learning yield
exampleSpecs.stakes: choose a curriculum of skills or repeat familiar work for more pay
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: skill-stack apprenticeship evaluates work by transferable capabilities
